name: Abhishek Bhardwaj
role: Member of Technical Staff, RL & Agent Infrastructure
bio: Abhishek Bhardwaj works on Agent and Reinforcement Learning Infrastructure at OpenAI. He builds systems that enable large-scale model training in RL environments, as well as secure and scalable cloud sandboxes for OpenAI’s agents. Before joining OpenAI, he created Arrakis, an open-source sandbox for AI agents. Previously, he worked at Google on ChromeOS and foundational microVM technologies, and at Replit on core infrastructure and early versions of Replit Agent.

positions.claim: Any sandbox primitive that shares the host kernel — fork/exec, containers, or gVisor — eventually allows an attacker to reach the host kernel; only hardware virtualization prevents this.
Startups building agent sandboxes should adopt micro VMs from the start rather than iterating through containers, gVisor, and V8 isolates.
Security should be prioritized over performance because system tricks can compensate for performance issues but not for a breach.
Seccomp filtering is a poor fit for open-ended agent products because you cannot know in advance which syscalls the workload needs, creating a bad feedback loop of blocked users.
The 'micro' in micro VM refers to the VMM's smaller footprint and faster boot, not to anything about the guest.
CrosVM was the first Rust-based VMM, and Firecracker was forked from it.
Disk persistence, not compute, is the next major unlock for agent sandboxes, turning agents from ephemeral executors into durable knowledge workers.
Snapshotting must be incremental at ChatGPT/Codex scale because saving full multi-gigabyte images every turn is financially and latency-wise infeasible.
Block-device access inside a micro VM is more efficient than shared-folder filesystem passthrough because it uses the guest cache and avoids exiting on every filesystem operation.
Checkpoint/restore enables harnesses to run Monte Carlo tree search over sandbox states across many days, backtracking and re-exploring.
Schedulers should score nodes by how many snapshot lineage layers they already have cached, reducing download time on restore.
Warm pools trade idle CPU and memory consumption for low creation latency, and a hybrid of warm pool plus memory-snapshot restore gets the best of both.
Giving models code execution was the key unlock for domains with verifiable rewards like math and code.
Running agents locally on laptops is a temporary state and the durable future is persistent, long-running agents in the cloud.
GPU-accelerated sandboxes are poorly served by micro VMs today, since VFIO passthrough cannot be shared across multiple tenants.
